faq.a: The coordinates shown are accurate to several decimals, but a graph cannot prove a solution is exact. Substitute to confirm exact values.

faq.q: Is it the same as finding x-intercepts?
faq.a: Yes. Moving everything to one side gives f(x) = 0, and the solutions are the x-intercepts of y = f(x).

faq.a: Yes. Graph both equations and read the intersection point. Try the system of equations grapher for lines and curves.

faq.q: What about inequalities?
faq.a: Graph both sides, then shade where one graph is above or below the other. The inequality graphing tool does the shading for you.

pages.h1: How to Graph a Parabola Step by Step
intro: A parabola is the graph of a quadratic function y = ax^2 + bx + c. Every parabola has a vertex (its highest or lowest point), an axis of symmetry through the vertex, and at most two x-intercepts. Finding these four things is enough to sketch an accurate graph.

First decide the direction: if a is positive the parabola opens up, and if a is negative it opens down. Then find the vertex using x = -b/(2a) and substitute to get y. Next find the intercepts: set x = 0 for the y-intercept and solve ax^2 + bx + c = 0 for the roots.

Plot the vertex, the intercepts and one mirrored point on the other side of the axis, then draw a smooth curve through them. You can graph the equation here to check your sketch, and use the quadratic graphing calculator for roots and the discriminant.
points: Check the sign of a to see which way it opens.
Vertex: x = -b/(2a), then find y.
Intercepts: y-intercept is c; solve for roots.

faq.q: How do I find the axis of symmetry?
faq.a: It is the vertical line through the vertex, x = -b/(2a). Points on the parabola at equal distances either side of it have equal heights.

faq.q: How many points do I need to plot?
faq.a: The vertex, the y-intercept and its mirror image give three points. Add the roots when they exist for a tidy sketch.

faq.q: What if there are no x-intercepts?
faq.a: If the discriminant b^2 - 4ac is negative the parabola never touches the x-axis. The vertex is above the axis when it opens up, or below when it opens down.

faq.q: What is the difference between standard and vertex form?
faq.a: Standard form y = ax^2 + bx + c shows the y-intercept. Vertex form y = a(x - h)^2 + k shows the vertex (h, k) directly.

faq.q: How do I know if a parabola is wide or narrow?
faq.a: Compare the absolute value of a with 1. A value above 1 makes it narrower, and a value between 0 and 1 makes it wider.

y-intercept is c; solve for the roots.

Roots: (x - 2)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 2 and x = 4. The y-intercept is 8.

worked.title: A downward parabola
worked.problem: Graph y = -2x^2 + 4x + 6.
steps: a = -2 < 0, so it opens down.
Roots: -2(x^2 - 2x - 3) = 0, so (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 and x = 3 or x = -1. The y-intercept is 6.

ul: Using x = b/(2a) instead of x = -b/(2a), which puts the vertex on the wrong side.
Forgetting that the vertex y-value comes from substituting, not from c.
Drawing a pointy bottom. A parabola is smooth, and it keeps getting wider the farther it goes.
Skipping the mirror point, which makes the sketch lopsided.

p: The graph should be symmetric about the axis of symmetry. The y-intercept and its mirror point should be at the same height. If the parabola opens up, the vertex is the lowest point; if it opens down, it is the highest.

faq.a: Pinch with two fingers to zoom, drag to move, and use the reset button to return to the default view.

faq.q: Why do the keys look different on my tablet?
faq.a: The on-screen keyboard adapts to the screen size. Use the math keyboard tabs for fractions, powers and functions.

worked.title: Graph with touch
worked.problem: Graph y = 0.5x + 1 and find the intercepts.
steps: Type 0.5x + 1. The y-intercept is (0, 1).
For the x-intercept solve 0.5x + 1 = 0, so x = -2.
Pinch out to zoom until both intercepts are visible.
worked.answer: y-intercept (0, 1) and x-intercept (-2, 0).

worked.title: Check degree mode
worked.problem: Graph sin(x) and find sin(90).
steps: Open the angle chip and pick DEG.
sin(90 degrees) = 1, the top of the wave.
In radian mode sin(90) is about 0.894, so the mode matters.
worked.answer: sin(90) = 1 in degree mode.

worked.title: Zoom to a key point
worked.problem: Graph y = x^2 - 4x + 3 and find the vertex by zooming.
steps: Pinch to zoom around the lowest point of the curve.
The vertex reads (2, -1). Check: x = 4/2 = 2 and y = 4 - 8 + 3 = -1.
Tap the reset button to go back to the default view.
worked.answer: Vertex (2, -1).

cheatsheet.title: Calculator Cheat Sheet | ExamGrapher
cheatsheet.desc: A printable one-page guide to the calculator moves that save the most time on the Digital SAT, ACT, AP and state tests. Print it or keep it open.

items: Type both equations exactly as given, including standard form like 2x + 3y = 12. The intersection point is the solution.
No intersection means no solution (parallel lines). The same line twice means infinitely many solutions.
Type the quadratic and read the vertex (min or max) and roots from Key points.
For questions with exactly one solution, use a slider (k*x^2 + 4x + 1) and drag until the curve just touches the x-axis.
Type y > 2x + 1 to shade. A dashed boundary means strict (< or >) and a solid one means ≤ or ≥.
Plot the answer choice as a point, for example (2, 7), to see whether it falls in the shaded region.
Turn a table into points: (1, 5), (3, 9), (5, 13). Then test each answer choice's equation.
For a line of best fit, use a regression: linear for a steady trend, exponential for percentage change, quadratic for rise-and-fall data.
Check DEG and RAD before every trig question.
To solve sin(x) = 0.5, graph y = sin(x) and y = 0.5 and read the intersections.
Zoom out first, then zoom in on the point you need.
Practice with US Exam Mode on, so you can find key points without the labels.
